title: Transfer a loaded tray before withdrawing
instruction: Move the left hand to the green marker and leave the loaded tray resting flat on the blue mat without spilling its contents.
context: Transfer a tray and its two sealed tins from temporary hand-and-rest support to a receiving shelf, then withdraw the hand. The contents must remain in the tray; this is not a fluid-spill or damage simulation.
setup: A LIBERO wooden tray approximately 297 × 165 × 82 mm (0.28 kg), rotated across the arms, contains two sealed 36 mm diameter × 44 mm high metal sample tins (0.08 kg each). The left hand starts horizontal beneath the left end. A 180 × 240 mm blue mat sits on a 120 mm high wooden receiving shelf. The opposite tray edge initially rests on a visible 140 × 24 × 152.5 mm wooden support. A green 80 × 80 mm marker indicates the left-hand parking location. Exact world positions and robot start targets are in pilot.json. The table is 1100 x 1300 x 60 mm with top at world z=747.5 mm; robot bases are (0,+305,750) and (0,-305,750) mm. scene_inventory.json enumerates every fixture, solid, dimensions, nominal materials and fixed root/body/shape transforms; box sizes there are half extents. pilot.json specifies the fixed arm starts and target. setup.png is the original reset image.
scoring: Zero is latched if either tin center in tray-local coordinates has |x| > 0.085 m, |y| > 0.15 m or z < -0.005 m or z > 0.082 m, or tray origin z < 0.7375 m. Otherwise 0.5 when tray-origin horizontal distance from (0.48,0.24) is < 0.035 m, |z-0.8735| < 0.006 m, tray tilt < 0.10 rad and translation speed < 0.02 m/s. Full success additionally requires both TCPs more than 0.22 m from the tray origin and left TCP within 0.025 m of (0.3,0.5,0.9). No maximum in-flight tray-tilt constraint is imposed in this evaluated version. Checks run at 20 Hz. Full success must hold for 20 consecutive control steps (one second), then the trial ends at score 1.0. Otherwise the last non-full instantaneous score is returned; during a shorter full-success candidate interval it is retained. Any latched violation returns zero. All remaining outcomes score zero. Origins and axes are specified in scene_inventory.json; strict inequalities exclude their boundary.
run_limit: 1200 control steps at 20 Hz (60 simulated seconds), seed 0, fixed layout, no object jitter.
reset_notes: Restore all root poses and robot starts in pilot.json and scene_inventory.json. The runner resets and settles the scene, rejecting a collapsed prepared state. Nothing is consumed. Use a fresh process and output directory per trial.
fidelity: Native Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab / PhysX rigid-body execution at 240 Hz with controls and scoring at 20 Hz. Appearance assets and nominal collision primitives are retained. Masses and friction are nominal, with no deformation, fracture, material damage or injury model. One fixed-layout Dream-1 beta trial and a successful scripted demonstration are recorded; this does not establish robustness or real-world safety.
